\subsection{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{steps}}}
\label{\detokenize{reference/d2edr2:steps}}\label{\detokenize{reference/d2edr2:d2edr2-steps}}
\index{steps (\$d2edr2)@\spxentry{steps}\spxextra{\$d2edr2}}\ignorespaces 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Type:} list\\
\sphinxstylestrong{Default:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0,\sphinxhyphen{}1}}\\
\sphinxstylestrong{Status:} current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)\\
\sphinxstylestrong{Sources:} input.txt; 08 t55; 08 t32a, t32b, t53, t65

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0,\sphinxhyphen{}1}} runs every step from 0 to 3N (or 6N) in a single run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first and last displacement steps to do in this run. The reference geometry is step 0, and the displaced
geometries are 1 … 3N (one displacement) or 1 … 6N (two displacements). This lets a numerical Hessian be split
across separate runs and then combined.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Not the same keyword as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$optimize steps}}. Tested in version 25 with water (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ridft}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{displace=1}}, steps 0\textendash{}9):
two partial runs (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{steps=0,4}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{steps=5,9}}) and a combining run with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{displace=1 steps=\sphinxhyphen{}1}} gave the same
frequencies, to within 0.4 cm⁻\(\sp{\text{1}}\), as a one\sphinxhyphen{}run Hessian with the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{displace=2}}. The combining run does no
SCF. Each part writes one numbered group per displacement (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$Energy000}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$Energy001}}, …) on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{num\textgreater{}}} lines. The collecting command in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{input.txt}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{grep "num\textgreater{}" … | sed "s/\textbackslash{}.*num\textgreater{}//g"}}) leaves the file names that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{grep}} adds at the start of each line;
the example uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{grep \sphinxhyphen{}h}} instead.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} 12\PYGZhy{}atom molecule, four inputs run in parallel on different machines:
\PYGZdl{}d2edr2 disp=1 steps= 0, 9 \PYGZdl{}end    \PYGZsh{} mol.in1
\PYGZdl{}d2edr2 disp=1 steps=10,18 \PYGZdl{}end    \PYGZsh{} mol.in2
\PYGZdl{}d2edr2 disp=1 steps=19,27 \PYGZdl{}end    \PYGZsh{} mol.in3
\PYGZdl{}d2edr2 disp=1 steps=28,36 \PYGZdl{}end    \PYGZsh{} mol.in4
\PYGZsh{} collect the partial results into one input:
grep \PYGZhy{}h \PYGZdq{}\PYGZca{}num\PYGZgt{}\PYGZdq{} mol.out1 mol.out2 mol.out3 mol.out4 | sed \PYGZsq{}s/\PYGZca{}num\PYGZgt{}//\PYGZsq{} \PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} mol.in
\PYGZsh{} in mol.in, replace the \PYGZdl{}d2edr2 line with the one below and run once more to process them:
\PYGZdl{}d2edr2 disp=1 steps=\PYGZhy{}1 \PYGZdl{}end
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{See also:} {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/Energy:energy-e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{E (\$Energy)}}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxstylestrong{Default:} \sphinxstyleemphasis{none stated}\\
\sphinxstylestrong{Status:} current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)\\
\sphinxstylestrong{Sources:} input.txt; 04 \#69; 02 \S{}5.7; 08 t34; 08 t57b

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reference shielding constants, indexed by atomic number, for computing chemical shifts. Values are needed
only for the elements present in the molecule.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A reference shielding is only valid for the method, basis set and grid it was computed with. A user input
posted on a forum has other TMS values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{standard(1)=31.3867 standard(6)=181.9781}}); the settings they were
computed with are not given. Compute TMS with
exactly the settings of the production run. Without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{standard}}, version 25 prints \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift=}} as minus the
isotropic shielding; with it, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift = standard − isotropic shielding}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{}nmr
 standard(1)=31.3915
 standard(6)=181.9921
\PYGZdl{}end
\PYGZsh{} computed for Si(CH3)4; usable for a series of hydrocarbons
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extra points in space, given as x,y,z triples, at which magnetic shielding tensors are computed in
addition to the nuclear centres. This is the way to compute NICS: NICS is the negative of the isotropic
shielding printed for the point.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{}nmr
 points=
      0.00000000    0.00000000    0.00000000
      0.00000000    0.00000000    1.00000000
\PYGZdl{}end
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\section{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{\$Energy}}}
\label{\detokenize{reference/Energy:energy}}\label{\detokenize{reference/Energy:group-energy}}\label{\detokenize{reference/Energy::doc}}
\index{\$Energy@\spxentry{\$Energy}}\ignorespaces 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Results of an earlier run (energy, gradient, Hessian, dipole data), read back as input.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program prints this group on lines prefixed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eng\textgreater{}}} (an energy, gradient or Hessian run) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{num\textgreater{}}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{num\textgreater{}}} lines come from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{task=dipole}} (one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$Energy}} group with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dx=}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ax=}}) and from numerical Hessians,
which write one numbered group per displacement: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$Energy000}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$Energy001}}, … (see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$d2edr2 steps}}). Strip the
prefix and append the groups to the next input. The helper script \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge}} on the official site does this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A stored Hessian is required for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$optimize saddle=1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{task=irc}}. It also speeds up difficult minimizations,
and it lets you redo vibrational analysis or thermochemistry (for example for other isotopes, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$thermo mass=}})
without recomputing.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
eng\PYGZgt{}\PYGZdl{}Energy
eng\PYGZgt{} E=\PYGZhy{}2.284057276940e+03
eng\PYGZgt{} D= 4.22290114e\PYGZhy{}08 \PYGZhy{}1.82061636e\PYGZhy{}08  2.32661117e\PYGZhy{}08
eng\PYGZgt{} G= 5.13271929e\PYGZhy{}06 \PYGZhy{}5.52234429e\PYGZhy{}06 \PYGZhy{}6.15997899e\PYGZhy{}06
eng\PYGZgt{}    ...
eng\PYGZgt{}\PYGZdl{}end
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\section{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{\$dynamic}}}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dynamic:dynamic}}\label{\detokenize{reference/dynamic:group-dynamic}}\label{\detokenize{reference/dynamic::doc}}
\index{\$dynamic@\spxentry{\$dynamic}}\ignorespaces 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Molecular dynamics with a thermostat.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Relevant when:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{task = thermostat}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Known from the official example inputs, a third\sphinxhyphen{}party input generator, the names in the version 25 executable
and one version 25 test. Only the meaning of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{file}} is shown by output; the rest is inferred.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In version 25, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{task=thermostat}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e=0.001 d=0.03 n=20,5 m=10 i=1}} ran with every tested theory (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dft}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ridft}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rimp2}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ccsd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tddft}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qm\_n3}}). The header echoes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e = 0.00100000}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dx = 0.03000000 L = 20,\sphinxhyphen{}5;10}}. The output has one line per step, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{point N: s … E … g …}}, where
negative point numbers are equilibration steps (the second value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}) and positive ones the production steps
(the first value). The official example (below) writes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{d=}} and the generator script writes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{h=}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v=}};
these are prefixes of the full names \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dx}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hb}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v1}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{}dynamic
 e=0.001
 d=0.03
 n=1000,100
 m=10
 i=1
 file=H40C20/H40C20\PYGZus{}\PYGZpc{}06d.qm.in
\PYGZdl{}end
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\section{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{\$uniq}}}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uniq:uniq}}\label{\detokenize{reference/uniq:group-uniq}}\label{\detokenize{reference/uniq::doc}}
\index{\$uniq@\spxentry{\$uniq}}\ignorespaces 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Duplicate\sphinxhyphen{}structure filtering over several \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$molecule}} blocks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Relevant when:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{task = uniq}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In version 25, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{task=uniq}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dist=0.01}} and several \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$molecule}} blocks in one input did no SCF. It listed each
structure as new (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1 =\textgreater{}     1}}) or as a copy of an earlier one with a distance (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2 =      1     0.0060421693}}),
printed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2 unique}}, and wrote the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atomic Coordinates}} of each unique structure. A copy of a water molecule that
was rotated and translated counted as identical (distance 0), and so did a copy with one H moved by 0.004 Å; a
copy with one H moved by 0.043 Å counted as a new structure.


\subsection{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{distance}}}

Threshold for treating two structures as identical: structures closer than this count as copies. The official
example uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dist=0.01}} on 157 MD snapshots, each in its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$molecule}} block. How the distance is measured
and in which units is not known. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dist}} is a prefix of the full name \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distance}}; the group also reads \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{file}}.
